newsitem.title: USA: CNG sees rising oil, natural gas production.
newsitem.headline: CNG sees rising oil, natural gas production.

text.p: Consolidated Natural Gas Co executives on Tuesday said the company's 1997 oil and natural gas production should rise from new wells on line this year.

The company is on track to produce 7 million barrels of oil and between 150 and 160 billion cubic (bcf) of natural gas in 1997, up from 4.8 million barrels and 147.5 bcf last year respectively, the executives said.
"We've been very aggressive in the (exploration and production) area and it's paying off for our shareholders," CNG Chairman George Davidson said at the company's annual meeting here.

Patrick Riley, president of the Pittsburgh-based company's producing unit, said the two wells at the Neptune deepwater spar are producing 14,600 barrels of oil per day (bopd), and a third well coming on line within a month will add 10,000 bopd.
"We will be close to the capacity of the Neptune spar within a month," he said in a presentation to reporters before the company's shareholder meeting.
The company holds a 50 percent stake in Neptune along with operator Oryx Energy Co and controls a 37.5 percent stake in the Popeye deepwater project operated by Shell Oil Co's offshore unit.
To supplement its rising offshore Gulf of Mexico production, CNG has stepped up onshore exploration and production along the Gulf Coast and in Oklahoma, he said.
Tests are due soon on an initial well in southern Oklahoma and a second well was spudded there, but he declined to disclose additional details on the prospects.
"There's some things going on there that I'd rather not let the whole world know about," Riley said.
